title: Recommendations released after inquest into police cell death
article: Saskatoon police detention cells may soon have paramedics in place 24 hours a day, seven days a week after a jury released its findings following the inquest into the death of a man in police custody.
Christopher Hiebert was 34 years old when he was found unresponsive in a detention cell on Sept. 9, 2009, just hours after he was arrested at his parent's home on fraud and theft charges.
He died shortly after at Royal University Hospital. A coroner determined he overdosed on pain and depression pills taken before he went into custody.
Last week's inquest analyzed the circumstances surrounding Hiebert's death. It ended with a jury making eight recommendations in hopes of preventing a similar death from happening again.
It requested mandatory, high-level CPR and First Aid training for all detention staff in case the paramedic on duty is busy.
In that case, the jury also recommended a sergeant should take over regular cell checks instead of a commissionaire.
Another proposed change is to implement a booking procedure that would include a consent form allowing paramedics access to prisoner's medical records.
